title: Transepithelial Iontophoresis-Assisted Cross Linking for Progressive Keratoconus: Up to 7 Years of Follow Up

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license-p>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

groups.description: 19 eyes of 19 patients aged 19-41 years with progressive keratoconus treated in 2013-2014; transepithelial iontophoresis-assisted CXL, riboflavin 0.1% with enhancers (Ricrolin+) delivered by iontophoresis at 1 mA for 5 minutes, UVA 10 mW for 9 minutes (5.4 J/cm2, UV-X 2000); prospective, non-randomized, single-centre study with follow-up to 84 months

exclusions.what: beta coefficients and p-values of the generalized linear model (Results text)
exclusions.reason: model estimates and p-values are not admissible values

notes: Five eyes met the article's progression criteria after a mean of 55 months (range 36-72); re-CXL (epithelium-off) was suggested for 4 of them and one patient required a corneal transplant. The article does not state whether these eyes were retreated or whether their later visits remain in Table 1; the series is kept as tabulated (one baseline, whole group, decreasing N).
Single-arm study without a declared experimental arm: role control.
Table 1 also gives age, CDVA, thinnest point, HOA, coma, spherical aberration and the A, B and C values of the ABCD progression display (not extracted).
